question: Charity Navigator eligibility rules in force at grant time: read archived copies (robots-checked archive host) of CN's methodology, release-notes and 'rating system' help pages as of mid-2023 and end-2024, list every eligibility clause that differs from the April 2026 text (DAF sponsors before the Spring 2024 note, any revenue floor, filing-count wording), and re-run mission_cn_eligibility_by_year.py with the dated rule set
conclusion_affected: Grant-time CN-eligible share of top-50 DAF dollars (72.66% central) and its comparison with the 76.85% current-status figure
rationale: The as-of test holds CN's 2026 rules fixed; the Spring 2024 release note shows DAF-sponsor ineligibility was added mid-period, which alone can move the share by up to 0.47 points, and other clause changes are unread

question: Within-year grant timing: replace the fiscal-year-end (72.66%) and fiscal-year-start (68.83%) bracket with an expected value, by weighting each sponsor-year's cut-off by a published monthly or quarterly DAF grant distribution (sponsor giving reports that state December or year-end shares) and, where sponsors publish dated grant lists, by actual grant dates
conclusion_affected: Point estimate of grant-time CN eligibility; FY2023 vs FY2024 gap
rationale: Grant dates inside a fiscal year are not public, so the result is a 3.8-point bracket; most dollars sit in June-year-end sponsor-years (61.7%) whose grants may cluster in December

question: Young large recipients: profile the top 50 recipients that are CN-eligible now but were not at grant time ($3.50bn; e.g. The 85 Fund, Just Trust for Education, Our American Future Foundation, City Fund, Murmuration Research Institute, Convergent Research): formation year, BMF ruling, NTEE, whether they are fiscal sponsors, pooled funds or c4-affiliated c3s, and what share of their revenue came from top-50 DAFs in their first returns
conclusion_affected: Why grant-time eligibility is 4.2 points below current status; DAF money to newly formed intermediaries
rationale: Organisations short of three e-filed returns at the year end account for 4.4 of the 4.7 points lost, and the largest are recent, large vehicles receiving $29-145m each; their nature is inferred, not checked

question: Recipients that stopped filing Form 990 after 2019-2021 while carrying BMF foundation code 10 (Compassion International, Convoy of Hope, Biblica, InterVarsity Christian Fellowship): count all top-50 recipients whose latest full 990 predates their latest 990-T or whose filings stop, with DAF dollars, and check from public statements or IRS determination data whether they obtained church or association-of-churches status
conclusion_affected: CN eligibility now vs at grant time ($0.17bn moves from eligible then to ineligible now); recipient transparency trend
rationale: These organisations were rateable at grant time but no longer file 990s, so current-status tests understate grant-time eligibility for them; the reason they stopped is not in IRS bulk files

question: Return availability lag: establish when TEOS XML batches were published (IRS TEOS download page history or archived copies, dated batch manifests) and how long CN takes to rate after a third return, to replace the processing-date cut-off and the FY-start proxy with a measured lag
rationale: XML_BATCH_ID months in the 2024-2026 index equal the processing month (median -11 days), so the index files give no publication date; CN's receipt date is not public
